I am very interested in space, astronomy, modern technology, and planetary exploration. My dream is to contribute to space science and work at NASA in the future.
I am currently developing KNK-1, a concept for an autonomous spacecraft powered by artificial intelligence, designed to explore Jupiter and its moons. I work on the concept, 3D modeling, space technology research, and presentation.
I want to build a team of people who share my passion for space, science, and innovation.

details:
KNK-1: Autonomous AI Mission to Jupiter
What it does and how it works. KNK-1 is a concept of a fully autonomous spacecraft powered by artificial intelligence. First, it studies Jupiter and analyzes how its weather conditions have changed over the past 5-10 years. Then it travels to Jupiter's moons. On each moon, the onboard AI evaluates the surface on its own. If it detects dangerous conditions, such as fire or lava, the spacecraft does not land. The spacecraft has six robotic manipulator arms, working in three pairs. In each pair, one arm does the main task and the second arm is its backup assistant, which helps if something goes wrong. Pair 1 touches and examines the surface. Pair 2 "smells" the environment. Pair 3 both "smells" and determines the chemical composition. The AI checks and verifies all results by itself. An onboard antenna transmits photos and documents to scientists on Earth using infrared light.
Benefits and expected impact. The spacecraft can make decisions, avoid danger and collect data without constant control from Earth. This makes exploration of dangerous worlds safer and more efficient.
Tools and software. The concept was developed using 3D modeling. The presentation was first created in Gamma and then completed in Microsoft PowerPoint. Text and translation were prepared with the help of an AI assistant (Claude).
Creativity. The idea combines AI decision-making with a "sense" system (touch, smell, chemical analysis) and paired backup arms for exploring dangerous worlds.
Factors our team considered. Communication with Jupiter is delayed, so the spacecraft must act on its own. Landing sites on the moons can be dangerous, so the AI must decide where it is safe to land.
